title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 4th District
area: South-central Tennessee, including Murfreesboro's southern exurbs, Tullahoma, and Fayetteville

context.text: Incumbent Scott DesJarlais (R) defeated Thomas Davis, Harold Jones, and Joshua James in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Victoria Broderick won a contested Democratic primary over Mike Cortese, Cliff Huffman, Tim Lanier, and Joyce Neal. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+11, and forecasters rate the general election Safe/Solid Republican. After the 2026 filing deadline reopened following Tennessee's new congressional map, the 4th District drew nine candidates in total, tied with the 6th District for the most of any Tennessee district.

candidates.name: Scott DesJarlais
candidates.ballotNote: Won a contested August 6, 2026 Republican primary

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (2025-2026), including its Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture and Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry subcommittees.
Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (2025-2026), chairing the Subcommittee on Strategic Forces and also sitting on the Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee.

candidates.researchNotes: His official site issues pages (desjarlais.house.gov) returned errors or no issue text when fetched, and no campaign statements on the priority issues were located; sponsored bills are added separately from congress.gov.

candidates.name: Victoria Broderick
candidates.ballotNote: Won a contested August 6, 2026 Democratic primary

priorities.text: Lists safety, affordability, and freedom as her core campaign themes.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she will work to codify abortion access into federal law and protect access to IVF and contraception.
positions.quote: I will work to codify abortion access into federal law

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she backs federal background check laws that close loopholes and funding for state red flag programs, while protecting responsible gun ownership.
positions.quote: I'll back federal background check laws that actually close existing loopholes, and I'll support funding for state red flag programs

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would strengthen the ACA and support a Medicare-like program for Tennesseans who fall in the Medicaid coverage gap.
positions.quote: In Congress, I'll fight to strengthen the Affordable Care Act by lowering premiums, reducing deductibles, and cutting out-of-pocket costs for families.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she will work to raise the corporate tax rate on the largest, most profitable businesses.
positions.quote: I will work to raise the corporate tax rate on the largest, most profitable businesses

priorities.text: Says he is focused on protecting workers and wages from AI and automation, and supports universal basic income and digital rights protections.

positions.summary: Says abortion should be legal as part of his reproductive health platform.
positions.quote: Abortion should be safe, legal, and rare.
By transitioning to a streamlined, single-payer framework, we eliminate the middlemen who profit from complexity.

positions.summary: Proposes a 42% corporate tax rate and a 50% rate on income above $500,000.
positions.quote: By adjusting the corporate tax rate to 42%, corporate revenue will double from $497 billion to $995 billion

positions.summary: Supports encouraging local zoning reform to allow more housing types.
positions.quote: we need to drastically increase housing supply by cutting federal red tape and incentivizing local communities to reform rigid zoning rules for starter homes, duplexes, and modern manufactured housing.
we must increase the minimum wage to $15 an hour

positions.summary: Lists ending U.S. tax dollars to Israel among his policy goals.
positions.quote: No More Tax Dollars To Israel

positions.summary: Says Congress should debate and vote on war.
positions.quote: Congress must reclaim its Constitutional duty to debate and vote on war.

statements.quote: Domestically, we must embrace a pragmatic energy portfolio that prioritizes the high-capacity, carbon-free potential of safe and modern nuclear energy.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Climate & Energy

statements.quote: We can enforce our laws and protect our communities by deporting criminals without resorting to reckless unaccountable enforcement tactics that put innocent people in harm's way.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Immigration & Border Reform

statements.quote: We must begin by offering universal pre-K for every family, giving children a strong developmental head start while providing working parents much-needed relief from skyrocketing childcare costs.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Education & Pre-K

priorities.text: Says his priorities are to improve public safety in every community, expand access to quality and affordable healthcare, and protect freedoms and opportunities.
Says he is committed to fighting corruption, including dark money in elections.

statements.quote: Healthcare options should be private decisions made with the advice of a healthcare professional and free from government oversight or control.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Healthcare Plan

statements.quote: And most of all some financial relief to help parents meet the changing financial demands of childcare while also helping upgrade facilities and salaries to keep up with the expectations of families and communities.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Childcare Plan

researchNotes: Scott DesJarlais did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey for 2026; his federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Jacob Anders and Clay Faircloth were researched from their own campaign websites; Faircloth's issue pages are brief and state no positions on most of the guide's issues. Clay Faircloth's platform comes from his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no 2026 campaign website was found. Biographies of Jacob Anders and Clay Faircloth rely on their Ballotpedia profiles and surveys; no campaign websites were found for them.
